claims.statement: A jointly selected sequence/depth/width architecture can improve both quality per training cost and quality per serving cost over strong conventional and hybrid baselines.
required_evidence: all retained components pass isolated policy-v1 promotion
final removal and pairwise interaction matrix
three-scale sign-consistent transfer including medium scale
realized training and production-runtime serving measurements
falsifiers: final candidate fails any hard quality floor
cost improvement disappears in the production runtime
architecture ranking reverses at medium scale or longer horizon
combined model is Pareto-dominated by a simpler ablation

claims.statement: A hierarchical sequence mixer can retain local detail, coarse global coverage, and precise retrieval with lower long-context cost than dense global attention.
required_evidence: retrieval, composition, position-binned loss, and independent long-context suites
prefill, decode, state, and peak-memory curves
falsifiers: loss or task non-inferiority fails
route or payload constituent retrieval fails
sparse selector misses required dense-attention support
theoretical cache/FLOP savings do not become realized cost savings

claims.statement: Content-dependent blockwise depth routing improves the compute-optimal depth/width frontier without unacceptable activation or serving complexity.
required_evidence: hidden-state, gradient, source-weight, entropy, and source-age analysis
checkpoint, export, prefill, decode, and activation-memory qualification
falsifiers: gain is inside the predeclared non-inferiority resolution
a retuned standard-residual depth/width point matches it
runtime or activation overhead exceeds its declared systems benefit
routing collapses to static or near-uniform weights without quality contribution

claims.statement: A stable latent expert design improves quality per active training FLOP without losing small-batch serving efficiency to expert memory or routing overhead.
required_evidence: dense-versus-MoE comparison with total and active parameter views
separate normalization, activation, and balancing ablations
expert load, routing margin, specialization, dropped-token, and outlier analysis
falsifiers: quality gain vanishes at equal wall-clock or memory budget
routing instability requires frequent rescue interventions
communication removes the active-FLOP advantage
small-batch serving is Pareto-dominated by dense SwiGLU

claims.statement: The selected sequence, depth, and width mechanisms provide complementary rather than redundant gains when combined.
required_evidence: all three pairwise interactions are measured
full combination beats every one-component removal
mechanism diagnostics remain healthy in the combined model
falsifiers: a negative pairwise interaction exceeds a component's isolated gain
the full model is tied by a simpler removal
one mechanism suppresses another's claimed diagnostic

claims.statement: The Speck candidate has a better empirical loss-compute frontier than the strongest conventional baseline over the tested scale range.
required_evidence: at least five compute-optimal scale points per architecture
shared fitting function and disclosed hyperparameter search
falsifiers: fitted advantage is not distinguishable under uncertainty
held-out point falls outside the predicted advantage
wall-clock frontier contradicts the analytic-compute frontier

claims.statement: The architecture's theoretical sparsity and compression produce realized end-to-end training and serving savings on named hardware and a production runtime.
required_evidence: at least one consumer and one datacenter hardware profile
falsifiers: custom kernels fail correctness or determinism contracts
scheduler, communication, or dequantization erases the claimed gain
benefit appears only in an unrepresentative microbenchmark

non_claims: A configured context length proves effective or usable context.
A lower analytic FLOP count proves lower wall-clock or dollar cost.
A collection of published components is itself a novel architecture.
One seed, one data order, or one training horizon establishes an architecture ranking.
A 150M proxy result automatically transfers to a billion-parameter model.
Post-training gains can be attributed to architecture when data or algorithms differ.
A whole-system comparison isolates every component.
